title: Technology Basics
description: How well do you know common tech terms, consumer devices, operating systems, and hardware?
seoTitle: Technology Basics Quiz – Test Your Tech Knowledge | AI Quiz Arena
seoDescription: Quick 10-question technology basics quiz covering CPU, RAM, SSD, Wi-Fi, and operating systems.

questions.question: What does CPU stand for in computer hardware?
questions.explanation: The CPU (Central Processing Unit) acts as the 'brain' of the computer, executing program instructions and processing data.

questions.question: Which company developed the Android mobile operating system?
questions.explanation: Google acquired Android Inc. in 2005 and officially unveiled the open-source mobile OS in 2007.

questions.question: What type of memory loses its stored data when a computer is turned off?
questions.explanation: RAM (Random Access Memory) is volatile memory used for active application data and empties upon power loss.

questions.question: What does 'USB' stand for in device connectivity?
questions.explanation: USB stands for Universal Serial Bus, an industry standard establishing specifications for cables and connectors.

questions.question: Which wireless standard is primarily used for short-range personal device connections like wireless earbuds?
questions.explanation: Bluetooth is designed for exchanging data over short distances between mobile devices, headphones, and peripherals.

questions.question: What does 'SSD' stand for in digital storage?
questions.explanation: Solid State Drives use flash memory with no moving parts, delivering significantly faster read/write speeds than mechanical HDDs.

questions.question: Which technology company produces the iPhone, iPad, and MacBook?
questions.explanation: Apple Inc. designs and manufactures iOS and macOS consumer electronics products.

questions.question: What does the abbreviation 'GPU' stand for?
questions.explanation: A GPU (Graphics Processing Unit) is a specialized electronic circuit designed to rapidly manipulate memory for image rendering and parallel computing.

questions.question: What is 1 Gigabyte (GB) equivalent to in Megabytes (MB) in binary standard?
questions.explanation: In computing binary units (gibibytes / gigabytes), 1 GB is composed of 1,024 MB (2^10 MB).

questions.question: What does 'HTTP' stand for in web addresses?
questions.explanation: HTTP stands for HyperText Transfer Protocol, the foundational communication protocol for the World Wide Web.
